study.title: Altered Small-World Efficiency of Brain Functional Networks in Acupuncture at ST36: A Functional MRI Study
study.study_design: within-subject crossover fMRI study; participants scanned before and after acupuncture at ST36 acupoint (ACUP) and sham point (SHAM)
study.randomization: presentation sequence of two runs (SHAM and ACUP) was randomized
study.blinding: subjects not informed of the order in which the two runs would be carried out; subjects instructed to keep eyes closed to prevent observation of procedures
study.inclusion_criteria: healthy, right-handed Chinese college students; aged 23-27 years
study.exclusion_criteria: medical history of any neurological or psychiatric conditions; naive to acupuncture; not previously exposed to a high magnetic field; subjects who experienced sharp pain (greater than two standard deviations above the mean pain level); one subject excluded for excessive head motion (larger than 2 mm and/or 2 degree in any direction)

conditions.timepoint_exact: before stimulation at SHAM; initial rest scan of 6 minutes
conditions.scan_context: resting-state fMRI scan before sham acupuncture
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Needle inserted perpendicularly to 15 mm depth, identical to the active acupuncture arm. At 15 mm, the needle reaches muscle/fascia, activating deep mechanoreceptors. This is full penetration despite being at a non-meridian point.

conditions.timepoint_exact: after stimulation at SHAM; 6-minute post-acupuncture scan beginning at 51 min
conditions.scan_context: resting-state fMRI scan after sham acupuncture; 25-minute resting period elapsed after needle removal before scan
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Identical insertion parameters to cond_be_sham: perpendicular insertion to 15 mm depth at nonmeridian points. The post-stimulation timing does not affect the physical depth classification. Full penetration into muscle/fascia confirmed.

conditions.timepoint_exact: before stimulation at ACUP; initial rest scan of 6 minutes
conditions.scan_context: resting-state fMRI scan before verum acupuncture at ST36

conditions.timepoint_exact: after stimulation at ACUP; 6-minute post-acupuncture scan beginning at 51 min
conditions.scan_context: resting-state fMRI scan after verum acupuncture at ST36; 25-minute resting period elapsed after needle removal before scan

interventions.stimulation_type: manual acupuncture with rotational needle manipulation
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: located four finger width below the lower margin of the patella and one finger width laterally from the anterior crest of the tibia
interventions.needle_size_exact: 40 mm long x 0.30 mm diameter supplied by Huatuo, Suzhou Medical Application Company
interventions.penetration_exact: needle inserted perpendicularly to the skin surface
interventions.manipulation_exact: needle manipulated rotationally with a flipping range of ±180° at a frequency of 120 flips/min for 1 min at 0 minutes, 7 minutes and 14 minutes
interventions.session_duration_exact: total experiment lasted 57 minutes: initial rest scan 6 min, 20 min acupuncture treatment, 25-min resting period after needle removed, 6-min post-acupuncture scan
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: one session per week; two sessions total (one ACUP, one SHAM) alternated each week
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: same experienced and licensed acupuncturist on all subjects
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: instructed to remain tranquil without engaging in any mental task; asked to keep eyes closed
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: ST36 is the most frequently used acupuncture point in Chinese acupuncture, especially for treating pain, hypertension, gastrointestinal and other physiological dysfunctions; emulated actual clinical practice of acupuncture in its entirety

non_acupoint_locations_exact: nonmeridian points 2-3 cm away from ST36

sham_details.sham_penetration_exact: penetrating (needle inserted perpendicularly to the skin surface to a depth of 15 mm)
sham_details.sham_location_exact: nonmeridian points 2–3 cm away from ST36
sham_details.sham_manipulation_exact: needle depth, stimulation intensity, and manipulation identical to that of ACUP group

sensory_interoceptive_responses.timepoint_exact: at the end of each fMRI scan
sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: None of the subjects experienced sharp pain after acupuncture
sensory_interoceptive_responses.between_group_difference_exact: no significant difference in the pain intensity measured by the VAS between ACUP and SHAM groups (P>0.05)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Sharp pain was considered to be an inadvertent noxious stimulation

sensory_interoceptive_responses.timepoint_exact: at the end of each fMRI scan
sensory_interoceptive_responses.instrument_name_exact: questionnaire based on a 10-point visual analog scale (VAS)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.item_or_subscale_exact: prevalence of various acupuncture sensations (soreness, numbness, fullness, heaviness, throbbing, warmth, coolness and any other sensations)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: The prevalence of various acupuncture sensations was expressed as the percentage of individuals in the group that reported the given sensations
sensory_interoceptive_responses.between_group_difference_exact: no difference between the ACUP and the SHAM groups in regards to the prevalence of acupuncture sensations (P>0.05)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: VAS scaled at 0 = no sensation, 1–3 = mild, 4–6 = moderate, 7–8 = strong, 9 = severe, and 10 = unbearable sensation

neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: resampled to 3×3×3 mm³ resolution; slices 30; thickness 4 mm; gap 1 mm; matrix 64×64; field of view 240×240 mm²
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 180 volumes per run (6 minutes per scan at TR=2000 ms); first 5 volumes discarded
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: graph theory analysis performed in custom code; ANOVA performed using http://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/6874-two-way-repeated-measures-anova
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: standard Montreal Neurological Institute space with the EPI image provided by SPM5 as a reference template
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: one subject excluded for excessive head motion (larger than 2 mm and/or 2 degree in any direction)
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: multiple linear regressions were performed to remove several sources of spurious variances arising from estimated head-motion profiles and global activity from each regional mean time course
statistical_thresholds_exact: P<0.05, corrected by false discovery rate (FDR) approach

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Small-world architecture of functional brain networks under each condition
contrasts.timepoint_exact: all four conditions (BE-SHAM, AF-SHAM, BE-ACUP, AF-ACUP)
contrasts.analysis_method_exact: graph theory analysis; comparison of local and global efficiency of real brain networks against matched random and regular networks across cost range 0.1–0.4
contrasts.direction_exact: local efficiency higher in regular networks than random; global efficiency higher in random than regular; actual brain networks located between curves of random and regular graphs
contrasts.notes: Brain networks exhibited small-world architectures under each condition. Networks also exhibited economical behavior since both local and global efficiency rose much faster than required wiring cost. At approximately 15% wiring cost, functional brain networks reached local and global efficiency of approximately 50%.

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Point and stimulation effects on global network parameters (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA on AUCs)
contrasts.contrast_type_exact: two-way repeated-measures ANOVA; point effect (ACUP vs SHAM) and stimulation effect (before vs after)
contrasts.analysis_method_exact: two-way repeated-measures ANOVA using integrated measures (AUCs)
contrasts.neuroimaging_metric_exact: Eloc, Eglob, γ (normalized local efficiency), λ (normalized global efficiency), σ (efficiency-based small-worldness)
contrasts.statistical_model_exact: two-way repeated-measures ANOVA with points (ACUP and SHAM) and stimulation time (before and after stimulation) as within-subject factors
contrasts.direction_exact: Neither the point effect nor the stimulation effect was significant on any of the five global network parameters (all P>0.05); significant point–stimulation interaction on local efficiency (F(1,17) = 5.66, P = 0.03)

extraction_notes.note: No MNI or Talairach coordinates are reported for any neural result. All neuroimaging findings are reported as ROI-level summaries using AAL atlas labels. No coordinate table exists. Coordinate fields left null throughout.
Coordinate space is not explicitly stated. The preprocessing used SPM5 and MNI normalization, but no coordinate space (MNI or Talairach) is declared for any result.

The paper describes 18 enrolled subjects divided into two groups of 9 (one for ACUP, one for SHAM), then alternated each week, making this a crossover design. However, n_total_analyzed is 17 after one subject excluded for head motion. It is ambiguous which arm the excluded subject belonged to; n_analyzed per arm cannot be determined.

Table 4 reports PCG.R (right posterior cingulate gyrus) showing ACUP > SHAM effect for nodal homogeneity, but the text states 'left posterior cingulate gyrus [PCG]'. This is an inconsistency between the table and text. The table value (PCG.R) was extracted as written in the table.

The paper states 'another 10 brain regions showed point main effects' (uncorrected) in addition to HIP.L (11 total), but Table 3 lists only 10 regions beyond HIP.L showing point effects. The text mentions '5 regions with increased nodal degree' and '6 regions with decreased nodal degree' which sums to 11, but the table lists only 10 additional regions (5 increased + 5 decreased, plus HIP.L = 11 total). There may be a discrepancy between the text count and table rows.
Expectancy was not formally assessed. The paper does not report any expectancy or credibility instruments or scores.

Individual deqi subscale scores (e.g., soreness, numbness, fullness, heaviness, throbbing, warmth) are not reported with means or SDs; only the aggregate statistical comparison between ACUP and SHAM is provided (P>0.05 for both prevalence and VAS pain intensity).

The sham acupuncture involves actual needle penetration to 15 mm depth at nonmeridian points 2-3 cm from ST36. This is a penetrating sham, not a validated non-penetrating Streitberger-type sham. The sham therefore involves active needling and potential deqi.

The paper states subjects were divided into two groups alternating each week, with 9 in ACUP and 9 in SHAM. This appears to be a crossover design where all 18 subjects ultimately received both ACUP and SHAM. The arm assignments as described may reflect the initial group assignment, not the total exposure. The total n analyzed (17 after one exclusion) participated in both conditions.
No clinical outcomes or behavioral performance outcomes are reported. The study is purely neuroimaging-focused in terms of outcome reporting.

The paper uses the term 'normalized nodal degree' in Table 2 for hub identification, but the methods section defines nodal degree (ki) as the number of edges linked to a node, without clarifying the normalization procedure applied to produce the values in Table 2.
Smoothing kernel details are not reported in the methods section.
The paper does not report flip angle or slice acquisition order explicitly for the fMRI sequence beyond 'axially' and 'flip angle, 90°' (flip angle is mentioned in methods: 'flip angle, 90°').
